questions.question: A time line is drawn with three jumps on it. It starts at 2:45 and the first jump lands on 3:00 (a jump of 15 minutes). The second jump goes from 3:00 to 4:00 (a jump of 1 hour). The third jump goes from 4:00 to 4:20 (a jump of 20 minutes). What is the total elapsed time from 2:45 to 4:20?
questions.explain: Add the jumps: 15 min + 1 h + 20 min = 1 h 35 min. The common trap is subtracting the digits (4:20 − 2:45 gives a fake 2 h 25 min); minutes are counted in 60s, so always hop to the next whole hour first.

questions.question: On a time line, a jump goes from 7:50 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. (10 minutes), then a jump from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. (1 hour), then a jump from 9:00 a.m. to 9:10 a.m. (10 minutes). How long is the whole duration shown on the time line?
questions.explain: 10 min + 1 h + 10 min = 1 h 20 min. Watch the first jump: from 7:50 to 8:00 is only 10 minutes, not 50 minutes, because an hour has 60 minutes and not 100.

questions.question: A time line starts at 10:40 and ends at 12:25. It is broken into three jumps: 10:40 to 11:00, then 11:00 to 12:00, then 12:00 to 12:25. The jumps are worth 20 minutes, 1 hour, and 25 minutes. What is the elapsed time?
questions.explain: 20 min + 1 h + 25 min = 45 min + 1 h = 1 h 45 min. A common trap is treating 10:40 to 11:00 as 60 minutes; it is 60 − 40 = 20 minutes, because the hour is finished at 60.

questions.question: A time line for a swim lesson has three jumps. Jump 1 goes from 3:55 to 4:00 and is worth 5 minutes. Jump 2 goes from 4:00 to 5:00 and is worth 1 hour. Jump 3 goes from 5:00 to 5:45 and is worth 45 minutes. How long is the swim lesson?
questions.explain: Add every jump, including the whole-hour one: 5 min + 1 h + 45 min = 1 h 50 min. Children often drop the 1-hour jump and answer 50 min, or count 3:55 to 4:00 as 45 min instead of 5 min.

questions.question: The bus from Coquitlam leaves at 4:25 p.m. and arrives at 6:05 p.m. How long is the bus ride?
questions.explain: Jump 4:25 to 5:00 (35 min), 5:00 to 6:00 (1 h), 6:00 to 6:05 (5 min): 35 + 5 = 40 min, so 1 h 40 min. The trap is borrowing 100 minutes from the hour instead of 60, which gives the impossible 1 h 80 min.

questions.question: Which method correctly finds the elapsed time from 7:50 p.m. to 9:15 p.m.?
options: Jump 7:50 to 9:50 (2 h), then take away 15 min, giving 1 h 45 min
Write 9:15 above 7:50 and subtract each column, giving 2 h 35 min
Jump 7:50 to 8:00 as 50 min (since 50 + 50 = 100), then 1 h, then 15 min, giving 2 h 5 min
questions.explain: Hop to the next whole hour, then count whole hours, then the leftover minutes: 10 min + 1 h + 15 min = 1 h 25 min. Column subtraction of clock digits is the classic trap, because 15 minutes cannot be taken from 50 minutes that way.

questions.question: A movie starts at 6:50 p.m. and ends at 8:35 p.m. How long is the movie?
questions.explain: Jump 6:50 to 7:00 (10 min), 7:00 to 8:00 (1 h), 8:00 to 8:35 (35 min): 10 + 35 = 45 min, so 1 h 45 min. Subtracting the clock digits (50 − 35) gives a fake 2 h 15 min, because the minutes cross into a new hour.

questions.question: Public skating at the Kamloops rink runs from 5:40 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. How long is the skating session?
questions.explain: Jump 5:40 to 6:00 (20 min), 6:00 to 7:00 (1 h), 7:00 to 7:10 (10 min): 20 + 10 = 30 min, so 1 h 30 min. Subtracting the clock digits (40 − 10) gives a fake 2 h 30 min, borrowing 100 minutes invents the impossible 1 h 70 min — an hour only holds 60 — and 1 h 20 min drops the last 10-minute jump.

questions.question: Noah's swim class runs from 4:50 p.m. to 6:35 p.m. His sister's class runs from 5:15 p.m. to 6:45 p.m. How much longer is Noah's class than his sister's class?
questions.explain: Noah: 10 min + 1 h + 35 min = 1 h 45 min; his sister: 45 min + 45 min = 1 h 30 min; the difference is 15 min. The trap is subtracting clock digits for Noah's class, which turns 1 h 45 min into a fake 2 h 15 min and makes the gap look like 45 min.

questions.question: Ava says the time from 7:45 a.m. to 9:20 a.m. is 2 hours 25 minutes, because 9 − 7 = 2 and 45 − 20 = 25. Which statement is correct?
options: She subtracted the minute digits the wrong way across the hour; the duration is 1 h 35 min.
She forgot that an hour holds 100 minutes, so the answer must be worked in hundreds; it is 2 h 15 min.
Nothing is wrong; subtracting the hours and the minutes separately really gives 2 h 25 min.
She should have borrowed 100 minutes from the hour before subtracting; the duration is 1 h 75 min.
questions.explain: Because 20 minutes is less than 45 minutes, you cannot subtract the columns; jump 7:45 to 8:00 (15 min), 8:00 to 9:00 (1 h), 9:00 to 9:20 (20 min), giving 1 h 35 min. Remember an hour is 60 minutes, so any borrowing takes 60, never 100.

questions.question: A class bus leaves the school at 8:40 a.m. and reaches the aquarium at 10:15 a.m. The class stays 2 h 30 min, and the ride back takes exactly as long as the ride there. How long is the whole trip, from leaving school to returning?
questions.explain: Each ride is 20 min + 1 h + 15 min = 1 h 35 min, so 1 h 35 min + 1 h 35 min = 3 h 10 min, plus 2 h 30 min = 5 h 40 min. The trap is subtracting 10:15 − 8:40 digit by digit to get a fake 2 h 25 min per ride, which stretches the whole trip by nearly two hours.

questions.question: The community library closes at 5:30 p.m. Emma starts her science project there at 3:45 p.m. and needs 2 hours of work time. Which statement is true?
options: Yes — she has 2 h 15 min, which is 15 min more than she needs.
No — she has 1 h 15 min, so she is 45 min short.
No — she has 1 h 45 min, so she is 15 min short.
Yes — she has 2 h 25 min, which is 25 min more than she needs.
questions.explain: Jump 3:45 to 4:00 (15 min), 4:00 to 5:00 (1 h), 5:00 to 5:30 (30 min): 15 + 30 = 45 min, so 1 h 45 min, which is 15 min less than the 2 hours she needs. Subtracting clock digits gives a fake 2 h 15 min and would wrongly tell Emma she has time to spare.
